verdict: Red 7/10 REJECT, blue 8/10 SUSTAINED (two findings reduced in severity, none overturned). The court was constructed around a single arithmetic threshold - Q2 provisions <=60bp of GMV refutes the bear - and the decisive finding is that the threshold is endogenous to a management financing choice. Klarna's own Q1-26 release (p.6, read multimodally by both benches) attributes the 0.55% provision rate partly to 'the increasing share of off-balance sheet receivables, reducing the need to recognize provisions on balance sheet'; $1.2bn of Fair Financing receivables were sold in Q1 for a $57m gain, against $68m of total adjusted operating profit. A sub-60bp print can therefore be manufactured by selling more receivables and a >65bp print can mean fewer sales rather than worse credit - the verdict axis adjudicates financing geometry, not credit. Two corroborating kills: ~84% of Q1 adjusted operating profit is gain-on-sale (and that same gain inflates the take-rate defense - ex-gain Q1 take is ~2.83%, so the 'scary' 28bp sequential drop is really ~11bp), and the p.7 vintage exhibits show 2025 US Fair-Financing 30+/60+ DPD curves sitting ABOVE 2024 at like quarters, in tension with management prose that delinquencies 'continue to trend down'. Blue reduced red's FATAL to SUSTAINED-but-readable: Q1 disclosed the components and introduced a supplemental reporting pack, so the 8/18 print will carry what is needed to rebuild a like-for-like rule - contaminated is not unreadable. Blue also correctly demoted red's SRT leg: the confirmed contaminant is forward-flow sales, not the SRT (which is typically synthetic, assets stay on-balance-sheet), though the thesis's claim that the SRT investor 're-underwrote on Q2 performance data' is invented - the PR states no data period. Under the response taxonomy this is a data/measurement kill of the decision rule plus a timing objection on entry (STARTER proposed at 93.9% of the 26-week high, +61% off the low), not a valuation objection. Nothing here is a dislocation: no forced seller or mechanism is named, KLAR is a heavily covered mega-IPO, and blue explicitly audited orphan discipline as inapplicable. What survives is not a position but a pre-committed, dated post-print re-entry rule for 8/18 requiring all three of: provisions/GMV <=60bp, disclosed receivable-sale volume at or below Q1's $1.2bn pace (else normalize before comparing), and 2026 vintage curves at or below 2025 at the same months-on-book. Any leg fails and the thesis is dead pending price. Growth itself is NOT refuted - ex-gain revenue is still ~+36% YoY with interest income +56% - so this is a rejection of the entry and the decision rule, not of the franchise.
